resume_brief: STANDALONE BRIEF — owner-directed 2026-10-09. His diagnosis: 'the stick-up model is in A-POSE not T-POSE, and that's why the arms are getting connected to the torso' + 'you're probably using the bullshit skeleton — use the good skeletons from our repos.' YOUR JOB: (1) VERIFY FIRST: load STICKUP_repaired.glb in Blender headless, measure the rest pose — arm angle from torso (A-pose ~30-45deg vs T-pose ~90deg). Confirm or refute his diagnosis with numbers. (2) SAVE THE REFERENCES: the Hardy taunt work (PR #58) needs its reference frames + methodology saved — pull the key video frames used for finger_guns/crucifix/hair_whip into tools/taunts/references/ as images + a METHOD.md documenting exactly how each clip was made (source video, timestamps, rotoscope process). If the frames weren't saved, re-pull them from the Hardy entrance video. Rank the top 3 candidates with evidence. (4) THE FIX: take the best path — either (a) re-pose Stick-Up to T-pose and re-run heat-diffusion skinning (A-pose bleed is a known rigging fact: separated arms = cleaner weights), or (b) transfer the best repo skeleton + its weights onto Stick-Up's mesh. Whichever you try, VERIFY with the probe renders at 15/30/45/60/90deg + the G4 deform metric — numbers, not eyeballing. (5) AUTOMATE IT: script the winning path open-source (Blender bpy) so any model gets the same treatment — this becomes part of tools/statue-to-game/. RULES: heartbeat THIS checkpoint every 15 min; branch -> PR, never direct to main; if his A-pose diagnosis is WRONG, say so with the measurements — don't fake agreement. Report: the rest-pose measurement, the skeleton ranking, which fix path worked with probe numbers, PR link.
